_comment: What CALL-E actually billed this account, read off the account's own usage page. These are first-party observations and not a published price, so they are here rather than in statistics.json, which holds figures with a public URL a reader can open. A district must confirm its own pricing before relying on any of it. There are two dated readings and they do not agree: `observed` is the flat 2026-09-04 period and `observed_metered` is the 2026-09-11 run, which billed between eight and fifteen times as much per call. Neither supersedes the other, because each is a true readout of the period it names, and the difference between them is the finding. tests/test_observed_price.py fails if the README or the page quotes a different number, and tools/money_across_runs.py puts the flat one beside the ceiling the run derives.

observed.account: the author's own CALL-E account, created for this hackathon
observed.surface: the Usage panel of the CALL-E dashboard, All countries, Date Range 2026-08-07 to 2026-09-07
observed.direction_note: The panel labels all ten rows IN. Every one of these calls was placed outbound by this software to a parent's number, so IN is either the panel's label for the leg CALL-E answers or a mislabel; the dashboard offers nothing that distinguishes them. It is reported because a reader checking this file would otherwise find a direction that contradicts the whole entry, and it is in the platform feedback for the same reason.
observed.period_note: This reading is bounded to the dashboard period it names. It was still the only reading available when every surface in this repository that quotes $0.05 was written. Calls placed on 2026-09-11 were not billed at this rate: see `observed_metered`.

what_it_supports: Every one of the ten rows on the usage panel is $0.05, and the period total of $0.65 divides by $0.05 exactly, so thirteen billable events were priced identically.
The durations on those rows run from 35 seconds to 1 minute 50, so the price did not move with the length of the call across that range.

Twelve of the thirteen have committed receipts from 2026-09-04. The thirteenth is a call this account placed outside the receipted set, and it is counted here because the period total is what the account was charged, not what the repository can show.
what_it_does_not_support: That $0.05 is CALL-E's price. CALL-E publishes no per-call price and this is one account's billing readout, on hackathon credit, in one month.

That the price is per call rather than per minute. Every observed call is under two minutes, so a flat $0.05 a call and a per-minute price rounded up to a two-minute minimum produce the same thirteen rows. Distinguishing them needs one call over two minutes, and this account has none.
That the price holds at volume, in another country, or outside a credit grant. Every row read IN, and the account was funded by a $1.00 top-up and a hackathon credit.

That $0.05 is still the price. Four calls placed on 2026-09-11 from the same account, the same software and to the same country billed 41 to 75 credits each, against 5 credits a call in this period. The change is observed and unexplained: the dashboard shows no rate card, no line-item breakdown and no effective date, so a repricing, the end of a promotional rate and an account tier change all fit it equally.
why_it_is_here: The entry published a ceiling for months and said, correctly, that no saving could be claimed because CALL-E publishes no price. A ceiling with no price beside it is a number a buyer cannot use. This is the price side, measured rather than assumed, with the three things it cannot tell anybody written down next to it.

observed_metered.account: the same account as `observed`, one week later
observed_metered.surface: the CALL-E dashboard, read after the benchmark run of 2026-09-11
observed_metered.credit_to_usd_basis: A +$10.00 top-up on 2026-09-09 credited 1,000 credits, so one credit is one cent. The earlier period cross-checks at the same rate: 13 events at 5 credits is 65 credits, and the panel showed that period as $0.65.
observed_metered.balance_reconciles: The account held 1,035 credits after the 2026-09-09 top-up, this run settled 252, and 1,035 - 252 = 783. The period cost of 317 is 65 from 2026-09-04 plus 252 from this run. Nothing is unaccounted for, which the 2026-09-04 reconciliation could not say.
observed_metered.duration_source: Measured from the WAV recording CALL-E returned for each call, with ffprobe. Not the dashboard's duration column. The API exposes no duration at all, and the panel's window and the recording's need not be the same, so the two are not conflated.

not_billed.zero_duration_failures: The SIP 500 and the SIP 480 placed in this run appear nowhere in the ledger. Six calls were placed and four were charged. CALL-E absorbs a drop originating in its own infrastructure and a line it could not reach.
not_billed.concurrency_rejections: 33 HTTP 429 `account_concurrency_exceeded` responses, counted off `bench-trace.jsonl`: 39 attempts to create a call, 6 accepted and 33 refused, with every refusal falling after the last acceptance. They returned no `call_id` and dialled nobody, and the ledger agrees. An HTTP 429 on this account costs nothing.

observed_metered.call_id_note: Rows are labelled with this project's own scenario ids. The platform call ids that join them to the dashboard are held with the receipts outside this repository: they are the key back to a recording of a real line, and tests/test_privacy.py fails if one is committed.

what_the_metered_reading_supports: The price is not flat. A flat per-call price bills a 53-second call and a 108-second call identically, and these billed 41 and 75 credits.

The price is not a per-minute rate with a two-minute minimum either. All four calls are under two minutes, so that reading also bills them identically, and it did not. The earlier file said separating those two readings needed one call over two minutes; four calls under two minutes with different lengths did it instead.
The granularity is coarser than a second. 1m32s over 23 turns and 1m36s over 25 turns both billed 68 credits.
Neither the zero-duration failures nor the concurrency rejections are charged, so a caller is not billed for CALL-E's own server errors or for its rate limiting.
what_the_metered_reading_does_not_suppor: Any rate card. Four calls cannot separate a per-second component from a per-turn one, because duration and turn count move together across all four. Credits per second fall as the call runs longer (0.77, 0.74, 0.71, 0.69), which is consistent with a fixed component plus a metered one and is four points, not a model.

Why the level changed. The dashboard shows no rate card, no line-item breakdown and no effective date, so a repricing, the end of a promotional or hackathon rate, and an account tier change all fit the same two readings.
That either rate holds at volume, in another country, or outside a credit grant. Both readings are one account, one destination, four and thirteen events.
what_a_buyer_cannot_do: Plan. An account cannot plan against a price it can only discover by spending, and cannot detect a change in it except by reading a balance. At 5 credits a call the desk time this project removes was worth several times the call. At 41 to 75 credits it is not: the twelve calls recorded on 2026-09-04 remove $0.39 a call gross and $0.08 net of the safeguarding work the same run creates, against a call now costing $0.41 to $0.75. That is the feedback, and it is the one item on this list a per-call cost field in the call object would close outright.
